content: Isoniazid is a medication used in combination with other drugs to treat active tuberculosis (TB) infections. It can also be used alone to prevent active TB in individuals who may be infected with the bacteria, such as those with a positive TB skin test. This antibiotic is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections like the common cold or flu. Take this medication by mouth on an empty stomach, either one hour before or two hours after meals, as directed by your doctor. For optimal results, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals. If you are on a weekly schedule, take it on the same day(s) of the week and at the same time. Continue taking this medication, along with other TB medications, for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve. Your doctor may also recommend taking vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) to prevent certain side effects, such as nerve problems. Isoniazid may interact with foods containing tyramine or histamine, such as cheese, red wine, and certain types of fish. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms. Your doctor may advise you to follow a special diet while taking this medication. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, or stomach upset. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, if you experience symptoms of an allergic reaction, such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Isoniazid has rarely been associated with severe, potentially fatal liver disease. The risk of liver damage is higher in individuals over 35 years of age, those who consume alcohol or use illegal injection drugs, or those with pre-existing liver conditions. Your doctor will likely monitor your liver function with regular tests while you are taking this medication. Avoid alcohol while using this drug, as it can increase the risk of liver problems. This medication may interfere with live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine, reducing their effectiveness. Additionally, liquid forms of this medication may contain sugar, so caution is advised if you have diabetes or a condition requiring you to limit sugar intake. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. While isoniazid passes into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may also interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine glucose tests, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. It is important to attend all medical and laboratory appointments while taking this medication. Lab tests, such as sputum tests, kidney and liver function tests, and complete blood counts, may be performed to monitor your progress and check for side effects. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. If you are on a weekly schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If you do not remember until the next day or later, consult your doctor or pharmacist for a new dosing schedule. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
